content.title: Miami (Ohio) basketball vs SMU prediction | Our pick for 2026 NCAA bracket First Four
content.text: March 15, 2026, 8:01 p.m. ETThe Miami RedsHawks are going to the NCAA Tournament for the first time in 19 years.Miami is in the NCAA Tournament as an at-large team for the first time since 1999, when Miami reached the Sweet 16 behind star Wally Szczerbiak.Miami will face fellow No. 11 seed SMU, an at-large team from the Atlantic Coast Conference.For the first time in 19 years, the Miami RedHawks are headed to the NCAA men's basketball tournament.Miami, in the tournament for the first time since 2007, earned an at-large bid to March Madness for the first time since Wally Szczerbiak led the RedHawks to the 1999 Sweet 16. Led by Mid-American Conference Coach of the Year Travis Steele, the RedHawks completed an undefeated regular season and entered Selection Sunday with a 31-1 record.The RedHawks weren't able to secure an automatic-bid from the MAC conference tournament title, but their impressive regular-season resume earned them a No. 11 seed in the Midwest region. It's Miami's 18th trip to the NCAA Tournament.Miami's first opponent in the Big Dance? It's 11th-seeded SMU, a member of the Atlantic Coast Conference which finished the regular season with a 20-13 record. The Mustangs, coached by Andy Enfield, were led all season by top-scorer Boopie Miller.Here's what to know about Miami's First Four matchup at UD Arena in Dayton, including our prediction for the final score.Buy Miami (OH) NCAA tournament tickets vs. SMUMiami RedHawks vs. SMU Mustangs scouting reportMiami has been one of the top offenses in the country all season, and their First Four matchup is with a similarly offensive-minded opponent in the SMU Mustangs.SMU likes to play high-scoring games, finishing second in the Atlantic Coast Conference in offense (84.2 ppg) but second-to-last in defense (77.6 ppg). Led by senior guard Boopie Miller's 19.2 points per game, the Mustangs have five players averaging double-digit scoring.Miami is a perfect mirror to SMU in many ways. Miami is second in the nation in scoring with 90.7 point per game, but the defense lags behind as the RedHawks allow 75.3 points per game. MAC Player of the Year Peter Suder leads Miami with 14.6 points per game, but the RedHawks get double-digit contributions from six active players.The biggest area of danger for Miami? SMU's offensive rebounding. The Mustangs 7-foot-2 center Samet Yiğitoğlu leads the rebounding charge as SMU averages over 12 offensive rebounds per game. The glass was a serious pain-point in Miami's MAC quarterfinal loss; the RedHawks will have to come out with much more physicality in Dayton.Miami RedHawks crowd advantage in First Four in DaytonJust an hour up the road from Oxford, Ohio, University of Dayton Arena should give the RedHawks a significant crowd advantage. With both teams having to make a quick turnaround for the Wednesday First Four session in Dayton, every little boost matters.Miami students are not yet on spring break, so a large number of students and local fans will likely be able to make the quick trip north. Miami head coach Travis Steele expected the crowd to be a major factor."Should be a home crowd for us, which I think will be an advantage," Steele said. "(Our students) are the pulse of our arena, so we need them to show up there in Dayton."Miami (OH) vs. SMU odds in NCAA TournamentNo. 11-seed Miami enters the first round as underdogs against 11-seed SMU. Despite the home court advantage for Miami, KenPom.com projects the RedHawks as 7-point underdogs against the Mustangs. The predictive site gives Miami just a 26% chance to win, with an anticipated final score of 86-79.Miami (Ohio) vs. SMU prediction: March Madness First FourThe biggest concern for the RedHawks will definitely be the physicality of the larger Mustangs. After getting pushed around by UMass in Cleveland in the MAC tournament, Miami will have to clean up its performance on the glass.Offensively, Miami should be able to go blow for blow with SMU. Each team can score in a variety of ways and should set up a high-scoring affair on March 18.SMU has not been great in road and neutral environments, going 5-10 in those environments this season. With a big Miami crowd expected to drive up to Dayton, the Mustangs should find themselves in hostile territory. SMU made the NCAA Tournament despite securing just one win in its last six games.In the end, I like the home court energy that the RedHawks should enjoy. The game should be a back and forth battle of high-powered offenses: I'll take Miami to beat SMU, 93-90, in UD Arena.
